title: The influence of heat conduction on propagating stress jumps
what_it_shows: The propagation of discontinuities of stress and temperature is studied in a one-dimensional medium in which the displacement and temperature fields are coupled (abstract, p.273).
why_it_matters: Supplies the classical statement of how conduction bleeds amplitude out of a stress jump at a wave front - the physical content behind the review's front discussion in Section 5.

title: A generalized linear thermoelasticity theory for piezoelectric media
what_it_shows: 'A theory of thermoelasticity for piezoelectric materials which includes heat-flux among the independent constitutive variables is formulated' (summary, p.39).
why_it_matters: The generalized route into piezoelectric media - the historical link the multiphysics chapter asserts without a source.

title: Thermodynamics of materials with memory
what_it_shows: Thermodynamics of materials with memory: fading memory, admissible processes and difference histories (contents page only).
why_it_matters: The origin of the memory-functional framework the memory chapter uses without citation.

what_it_shows: Not read: identified from the Crossref record only (Compte 1997, The generalized Cattaneo equation, J. Phys. A 30:7277)

title: Numerical inversion of Laplace transforms using a Fourier series approximation
what_it_shows: 'A method is presented for numerically inverting a Laplace transform that requires, in addition to the transform function itself, only sine, cosine, and exponential functions' (abstract, J. ACM 23, 89).
why_it_matters: A standard inversion method missing from the methods list.

title: On the existence and the asymptotic stability of solutions to the equations of linear thermoelasticity
what_it_shows: Existence, differentiability and asymptotic stability of solutions of the mixed initial-boundary value problem of linear thermoelasticity (contents page p.241 lists a section on 'Existence and Differentiability of Solutions').
why_it_matters: The review says the classical coupled theory is asymptotically stable with diffusive decay; this is the theorem that should carry that sentence.

title: Plane waves in a thermoelastic solid
what_it_shows: 'In an isotropic, thermoelastic solid shear waves are unaltered by thermal effects. However, two distinct dilatational waves exist, both of which are dispersed and attenuate' (abstract, p.204).
why_it_matters: The two-dilatational-wave result that the review's dispersion table generalises; without it the classical-limit column has no cited source.

what_it_shows: Not read: identified from the Crossref record only (Ezzat 2011, Theory of fractional order in generalized thermoelectric MHD - not the Ezzat entry in the bib)

authors: Gurtin, M. E.; Pipkin, A. C.
title: A general theory of heat conduction with finite wave speeds
what_it_shows: A general theory of heat conduction with finite propagation speed; it opens from the observation that the classical parabolic equation 'has a very unpleasant feature: a thermal disturbance at' one point is felt everywhere at once (introduction, p.113).
why_it_matters: The third historical route to finite-speed conduction alongside Cattaneo and the LS/GL theories; the review's history jumps from Cattaneo to LS without it.

title: Method of Lagrange multipliers for exploitation of the entropy principle
what_it_shows: Introduces the Lagrange-multiplier technique for imposing the entropy principle on constitutive relations instead of case-by-case manipulation (introduction, p.131).
why_it_matters: The method behind every constitutive restriction quoted in Section 3; the review uses the Coleman-Noll era results without citing its generalisation.

authors: Mindlin, R. D.; Eshel, N. N.
title: On first strain-gradient theories in linear elasticity
what_it_shows: 'This paper contains a study of the linear theory of elasticity in which the potential' energy depends on the strain and its first gradient (abstract, p.109).
why_it_matters: The canonical first strain-gradient formulation behind the gradient-elasticity subsection.

title: Thermoelastic waves in solids with thermal relaxation
what_it_shows: 'Maxwell's modified heat conduction equation is used to study plane harmonic waves in unbounded media as well as in' layered media (summary, p.53).
why_it_matters: The first systematic plane-harmonic-wave study of a relaxation theory; the review's LS/GL dispersion reproduces its setting without citing it.

title: Plane waves in thermoelasticity and magnetothermoelasticity
what_it_shows: 'An exact solution of the frequency equation for plane thermoelastic waves is given. The solutions for large and small frequencies and for small coupling' are developed (abstract, p.467).
why_it_matters: An exact frequency equation for the classical theory, a benchmark for the review's asymptotics.

title: Non-Fourier phonon heat conduction at the microscale and nanoscale
what_it_shows: A review of the non-Fourier conduction regimes - Casimir-Knudsen, hydrodynamic (second sound), coherent/localization, low-dimensional divergence - that 'critically assess[es] experimental evidence for each regime' (abstract, Nature Reviews Physics 3, 555).
why_it_matters: The best modern map of which non-Fourier regimes have experimental support; Section 9 currently rests on individual papers instead.
